title: Chirp's Grey Puddle
markdown:
Chirp the chick popped out of his nest ready for a super fun day. The sunshine felt warm and tickly on his fuzzy yellow fluff. His favorite place in the whole meadow was the big puddle by the Whispering Willow. Most days it shimmered red like ladybugs, blue like tiny flower petals, yellow like yummy buttercups. It would wiggle and jiggle as if it knew a happy dance.

Today the puddle was grey. Just grey, like a forgotten cloud that had dropped all its colors. Chirp tilted his head.

“Where did the pretty colors go?”

He felt a little wobbly inside, as if his tummy had lost its bounce. He hop-hopped closer. His feet went pitter-patter on the grass.

“Peep?” he whispered to the dull water.

He hopped once and splished. A bead of grey landed on a daisy. The puddle stayed grey. His little chest felt floppy, like a balloon that had lost its air. He sat down with a sigh.

On a sunny patch of moss, fast asleep, lay Nimbus the nap dragon. Big and soft, the color of a gentle rain shower. Nimbus loved shiny things, especially for naps. His scales twinkled like dewdrops on a web even while he snoozed.

Chirp tiptoed over.

“Nimbus. Psst. Wakey-wakey.”

Long eyelashes fluttered open like slow curtains.

“Mmmph?” A puff of sleepy air smelled like warm sunshine and sweet dreams.

“The puddle is all grey. The colors are gone.”

Nimbus yawned. It sounded like a breeze in the willow.

“Grey? Oh dear. Grey needs a sparkle. A shimmy. Let’s make it shine.” His eyes were the color of a clear night sky. “Shiny pebbles. They make my nap spot twinkly. Come on, little Chirp. Let’s find some.”

He stretched his cloud-soft body. Wings gave a gentle flutter. “Shhh,” he whispered, like a lullaby. Chirp’s wobbly tummy felt bouncy again.

They waddled and fluttered past the willow’s long hair to a happy babbling brook. Wow. Sparkly stones were scattered everywhere, like little fallen stars. Some glittered like tiny diamonds. Some shone like little round moons. Chirp turned over a dull one with his foot and left it. He wanted only the ones that already knew how to wink. He picked up a beakful of the brightest. Nimbus nudged a few more with his soft cloud-nose, very carefully, as if each pebble might still be dreaming.

They trotted back to the sad grey puddle.

“Ready?” Nimbus rumbled.

Chirp nodded so fast his fluff bounced.

“One, two, three.”

They dropped the pebbles in.

Plink. Plink. Sparkle-ding.

The grey melted away like magic. Swirls of happy red, bright blue, sunny yellow, and soft green danced and twirled. The puddle was a rainbow puddle again. It sparkled and winked in the sun, as happy as could be. The willow’s leaves found their colors in the water.

Chirp did a happy hop. His fluffy tail wiggled.

“Thank you, Nimbus. It’s beautiful again.”

Nimbus curled up by the water. His scales caught the new rainbow light. He did not say shiny pebbles make everything better. He only mumbled something half a nap already, eyes drooping, and Chirp stood in the wet grass watching the willow’s reflection get its colors back, one ripple at a time, until even the daisy with the grey splash looked like itself again.
